PERF-001.name: N+1 Query Pattern
PERF-001.question: Does this function issue a database or API query inside a loop over the results of an earlier query, one round trip per item?

any: a loop over fetched rows or records calls a query, find, get or HTTP request for each element
a lazily loaded relation or attribute is accessed per item inside the loop, triggering a fetch each time
python: an ORM loop accesses a related field per object, such as obj.author.name, without select_related or prefetch_related
javascript: await inside a for loop calls a repository, fetch or SQL query keyed by each item's id
typescript: a TypeORM or Prisma call such as findOne or findUnique is awaited inside a for...of over earlier results, or a lazy relation is awaited per item

any: related data is loaded up front with a join, IN clause, batch request or eager loading
the loop works only on data already in memory
the loop runs over a small fixed set, such as a handful of configuration keys
typescript: related rows are loaded in one query with relations or include, or ids are batched with In() or a where id in filter

distinguish_from.PERF-002: a single query loads too much data rather than many small queries

PERF-002.name: Unbounded Data Loading
PERF-002.question: Does this function load an entire table, collection or result set into memory with no limit, pagination or streaming?

any: a SELECT with no LIMIT or WHERE, or a find all or list call with no page size, is fully materialised
an API or storage listing is read in full into a list or array before processing
python: calls such as .all(), fetchall(), list(queryset) or read() of a whole file load everything at once
javascript: find({}) or findAll() with no limit, or toArray() on a whole cursor, is used
typescript: repository.find() or prisma.model.findMany() is called with no take, cursor or narrowing where clause

any: the query has a limit, page size, cursor, keyset pagination or a bounded filter
results are streamed or iterated in batches without collecting them all
the data source is known to be small and fixed, such as an enum table
typescript: the query passes take and skip or a cursor, or rows are streamed in batches

distinguish_from.PERF-001: many queries are issued per item rather than one oversized query

PERF-003.name: Missing Database Index on Filtered Column
PERF-003.reason: Depends on the database schema's indexes, which are not in the function's code.

PERF-004.name: Inefficient String Concatenation in Loop
PERF-004.question: Does this function build a string by repeated concatenation inside a loop?

any: inside a loop, a string variable is extended with += or s = s + ... on each iteration
javascript: a string is grown with += across loop iterations that can run many times
python: a str is grown with += in a for or while loop

any: parts are collected into a list or array and joined once after the loop
a builder or buffer is used, such as io.StringIO, a String with push_str, or std::string with reserve and append
the loop has a small fixed number of iterations
rust: push_str or write! onto a String, which grows in amortised constant time

distinguish_from.PERF-006: the cost comes from recomputing the same value on each iteration rather than from copying a growing string

PERF-005.name: Blocking I/O in Hot Path
PERF-005.question: Does this function make a blocking network, disk or subprocess call while acting as a request handler, event loop callback or tight loop body?

any: a request handler, async function or per-frame or per-message callback performs synchronous file, socket or subprocess I/O
a sleep or blocking wait runs on a request or event-loop path
javascript: readFileSync, writeFileSync, execSync or other *Sync calls run inside a server handler or async function
python: an async def calls requests, time.sleep, open().read or subprocess.run without awaiting a non-blocking version
rust: an async fn calls std::fs, std::net, std::thread::sleep or Command::output without spawn_blocking

any: the I/O is asynchronous and awaited, or moved to a worker thread or blocking pool
the call runs only at start-up, in a CLI tool or batch script, or in tests

distinguish_from.PERF-008: the repeated call could be cached rather than the call being blocking

PERF-006.name: Redundant Repeated Computation
PERF-006.question: Does this function recompute an expensive result that never changes between calls, such as compiling a regex or building a lookup table, on every call or loop pass?

any: a regular expression is compiled, a configuration file parsed or a lookup table built inside the function or a loop with constant inputs
a loop recomputes the same value each pass, such as a length, hash or derived key that does not depend on the loop variable
python: re.compile, json.loads of a constant or a large dict literal is built inside a frequently called function
javascript: new RegExp with a constant pattern or JSON.parse of a constant runs inside a handler or loop

any: the result is computed once at module level, in a static or lazy initialiser, or cached
the inputs vary between calls, so the work is not redundant
the computation is cheap, such as simple arithmetic or a literal regex the runtime caches

distinguish_from.PERF-008: the repeated work is an external request rather than a pure computation

PERF-007.name: Inefficient Membership Test on Sequence
PERF-007.question: Does this function repeatedly test membership or search for keys in a list or array inside a loop, where a set or map would make each lookup constant time?

any: inside a loop, x in list, list.index, Array.includes, indexOf, find or a nested loop searches a sequence that grows with the input
the lookup is against a set, dict, map or hash table
the searched sequence is small and fixed, such as a literal of a few items
the membership test runs once rather than per iteration

distinguish_from.PERF-006: the repeated work is a computation unrelated to searching a sequence

PERF-008.name: Missing Cache on Expensive Repeated Request
PERF-008.question: Does this function repeat an expensive external call or lookup for the same inputs without any cache or memoisation?

any: a loop or per-request path fetches the same reference data, permission or feature flag with unchanged arguments
the same remote call or query appears more than once in the function with identical inputs
results are cached in a map, memoisation decorator, request-scoped cache or shared cache layer
the value is fetched once and reused for the rest of the function
freshness matters, such as a balance or lock state, so repeating the call is intended

distinguish_from.PERF-006: the repeated work is a local pure computation rather than an external call

PERF-009.name: Subnormal Floating-Point Values Slowing Hot Numeric Loops
PERF-009.question: Does a tight numeric loop in this function repeatedly compute with floating-point values that can decay towards zero into the subnormal range?

any: a loop repeatedly multiplies a value by a factor below one (decay, damping, filter feedback) with no flush to zero
an iterative filter, reverb, physics or probability update whose state shrinks towards zero without a threshold
very small probabilities or weights multiplied together in a loop instead of working in log space
values below a small threshold are set to zero, or a tiny offset is added, each iteration
the code enables flush-to-zero or denormals-are-zero mode before the loop
the arithmetic is integer or fixed point, or probabilities are kept in log space
python: the work is ordinary Python floats in a non-hot loop where interpreter overhead dominates

distinguish_from.CWE-1050: the loop is slowed by acquiring platform resources rather than by floating-point values

PERF-010.name: Exact or Arbitrary-Precision Arithmetic in Hot Numeric Paths
PERF-010.question: Does this function do exact rational or arbitrary-precision arithmetic inside a loop where the operand sizes keep growing and bounded floating point would serve?

any: a loop repeatedly multiplies or adds fractions or big integers, accumulating into the same exact value
an iterative numeric method (series, simulation, matrix step) carried out in exact or unbounded types
python: fractions.Fraction or decimal.Decimal with a large precision used as an accumulator in a hot loop
javascript: BigInt or a big-number or rational library used for repeated accumulation inside a loop
c: GMP mpq_t or mpz_t, or MPFR at high precision, updated repeatedly in a loop
cpp: boost::multiprecision cpp_int or cpp_rational, or GMP mpq_class or mpz_class, updated repeatedly inside a loop
rust: num::BigRational, BigInt or similar arbitrary-precision types accumulated in a loop

any: exact types are used only once or a fixed few times, not in a loop
the exactness is required, such as money, cryptography or exact combinatorics, and values are rounded or reduced each step
ordinary fixed-width integers or floating point are used

PERF-011.name: Front Insertion or Removal on an Array-Backed Sequence in a Loop
PERF-011.question: Does a loop in this function repeatedly insert at or remove from the front of a contiguous list, array or vector, shifting all remaining elements each time?

any: a loop over input-sized data takes items from index 0 or adds items at index 0 of an array-backed sequence
python: list.pop(0), list.insert(0, x) or del lst[0] inside a while or for loop
javascript: array.shift() or array.unshift(x) inside a loop that runs once per item, such as a queue drained with while (queue.length)
cpp: vec.erase(vec.begin()) or vec.insert(vec.begin(), x) on a std::vector inside a loop
rust: Vec::remove(0) or Vec::insert(0, x) inside a loop

any: the sequence is a deque or linked structure with constant-time front operations
the sequence is small and bounded by a constant, or the front operation runs once outside any loop
python: collections.deque with popleft or appendleft
cpp: std::deque or std::list
rust: VecDeque with pop_front or push_front

distinguish_from.PERF-007: the repeated cost is searching a sequence for a value, not shifting elements

PERF-012.name: Independent Async Operations Awaited One at a Time in a Loop
PERF-012.question: Does this function await independent asynchronous calls one after another inside a loop, so each waits for the previous one to finish?

javascript: await fetch, a database call or another promise inside for or for...of, where no iteration uses an earlier iteration's result
python: await of an aiohttp, httpx, database or other coroutine inside a for loop over independent items
rust: .await on a request or I/O future created per item inside a for or while loop over independent items

any: each iteration depends on the result of the previous one, such as pagination with a cursor or ordered writes
the loop deliberately serialises calls to respect a rate limit or ordering requirement stated in the code
the loop runs a small fixed number of times
javascript: promises are collected and awaited with Promise.all, Promise.allSettled or a concurrency limiter
python: coroutines are gathered with asyncio.gather, TaskGroup or a semaphore-limited pool
rust: futures are combined with join_all, FuturesUnordered, buffer_unordered or spawned tasks

distinguish_from.PERF-001: each request in the loop is driven by rows from an earlier query, an N+1 pattern
distinguish_from.PERF-005: the call blocks the thread rather than awaiting asynchronously

PERF-013.name: Container Grown Element by Element Without Reserving Known Capacity
PERF-013.question: Does this function grow a buffer or vector one element at a time inside a loop when the final size is already known, so it reallocates and copies repeatedly?

c: realloc(buf, (n + 1) * size) or realloc by a fixed small increment inside a loop that appends one item per pass
cpp: push_back or emplace_back in a loop over a container or count of known size, with no reserve before the loop
rust: Vec::new() or String::new() followed by push or push_str in a loop over a known length, with no with_capacity or reserve

any: the final size is not known before the loop and the container grows geometrically
the loop appends only a few items
c: the buffer size is doubled or multiplied on each growth, or allocated once at its final size
cpp: reserve(n) or a sized constructor is called before the loop
rust: Vec::with_capacity, reserve, or collect() from an iterator with a known size hint

distinguish_from.PERF-004: the repeated growth is string concatenation that creates a new string each time
distinguish_from.CWE-1325: the allocations are not bounded overall, rather than merely repeated

PERF-014.name: Large Value Copied Where a Borrow or Reference Would Do
PERF-014.question: Does this function copy a large structure, string or container by value when it only reads it, such as a by-value parameter, a copying loop variable or a clone?

c: a parameter of a large struct type, such as one holding arrays, passed by value and only read
cpp: a std::vector, std::string, std::map or large class parameter taken by value and only read, with no std::move of it
for (auto x : container) over strings, vectors or large objects that are only read
rust: a String, Vec or large struct is cloned inside a loop or on each call where the clone is only read and a reference would compile

any: the value is small, such as an integer, pointer or a struct of a few scalar fields
c: the struct is passed through a pointer to const
cpp: the parameter is const T& or a view such as std::string_view or std::span
the by-value parameter is moved into storage, the sink idiom
rust: the function borrows with &T or &[T], or the clone is needed because the value is moved into another owner

distinguish_from.CWE-1176: the waste is repeated computation rather than copying data

PERF-015.name: Deep Copy Through a Serialisation Round Trip
PERF-015.question: Does this function make a copy of an object by serialising it and immediately parsing the result back?

javascript: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) used to clone an object or array
python: json.loads(json.dumps(obj)) or pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(obj)) used to clone

any: the serialised form is sent, stored or validated, not just parsed straight back
the round trip runs once on small configuration data at start-up
javascript: structuredClone, a spread copy or a library deep clone is used
python: copy.copy, copy.deepcopy or a constructor copy is used

PERF-016.name: Exceptions Thrown for Expected Outcomes Inside a Hot Loop
PERF-016.question: Does a loop in this function throw and catch an exception for a routine case that occurs on many iterations, such as a missing key or bad item?

any: a try block inside a loop over input-sized data whose handler is expected to run for a large share of items, such as skipping invalid entries
cpp: std::stoi, at() or a custom throw caught inside the loop to skip items, or throw used to break out of a loop
javascript: throw and catch used inside a loop to skip items or to exit early from iteration
python: raise inside a loop to signal a common case, caught in the same loop

any: the exception handles a genuinely rare failure such as an I/O error
the loop runs a small fixed number of times
the routine case is tested with a branch or non-throwing call before the operation
python: a try/except around a lookup where the exception is expected only rarely, which is idiomatic and cheap when nothing is raised
cpp: std::from_chars, find, count or an error code is used instead of a throwing call

distinguish_from.CWE-390: the exception is caught and ignored as an error-handling failure, not a speed problem

PERF-017.name: Unbuffered Small Reads or Writes Inside a Loop
PERF-017.question: Does a loop in this function read or write data in very small pieces through an unbuffered file, socket or stream, making a system call for each one?

any: a loop issues one read or write call per byte, character, record or line on a handle that does no buffering
c: read(fd, &c, 1) or write(fd, buf, 1) inside a loop on a raw descriptor
cpp: std::endl or std::flush on std::cout or a std::ofstream inside a loop, forcing a flush for every line
python: writes per item to a file opened with buffering=0, or os.write per item inside a loop
javascript: fs.writeSync, fs.appendFileSync or fs.readSync called once per line or item inside a loop
rust: write or read calls per item on File, TcpStream or stdout without BufWriter, BufReader or a lock held for the loop

any: the handle is buffered, or output is collected and written once
the loop runs a small fixed number of times
c: stdio streams such as fwrite, fputc or fprintf, which buffer by default
cpp: the loop writes '\n' to a std::ofstream or std::cout, so the stream buffer collects the output
rust: the handle is wrapped in BufWriter or BufReader, or stdout().lock() is taken before the loop

distinguish_from.PERF-005: the problem is that the call blocks a request handler or event loop, not the number of calls
distinguish_from.CWE-1050: the per-iteration cost is acquiring a resource such as a connection or lock, not unbuffered I/O

PERF-018.name: Expensive Log Message Arguments Built When the Level Is Disabled
PERF-018.question: Does this function build costly debug or trace log messages, such as serialising objects or calling helpers, even when that log level may be disabled?

any: a debug, trace or verbose log call whose argument serialises a large object, joins a collection or calls an expensive function, in a loop or frequently called path
python: logger.debug(f"...{expensive(x)}...") or logger.debug("%s" % json.dumps(obj)) where formatting happens before the call
javascript: logger.debug(`...${JSON.stringify(obj)}`) or console.debug with a serialised payload in a hot path
rust: format! or to_string called to build a String that is then passed to a debug! or trace! macro
c: snprintf of a debug message into a buffer before a call that checks the log level
cpp: a debug message built with std::ostringstream, std::to_string or std::format, or an argument calling dump() or a serialiser, before the level is checked

any: the message uses only cheap values such as plain variables or literals
the call is guarded by an explicit level check
the log call runs rarely, such as once at start-up or on an error path
cpp: only cheap arguments are passed to a lazy formatting call such as spdlog::debug("{}", x), which formats only when the level is enabled
python: logger.debug("... %s", value) with lazy argument formatting
rust: arguments are passed directly to log or tracing macros, which skip evaluation when the level is off

PERF-019.name: Rows Fetched Only to Count Them or Test Existence
PERF-019.question: Does this function load all matching rows or documents from a data store only to count them or check whether any exist?

any: a query returns every matching record and the code then uses only its length or tests whether it is empty
python: len(Model.objects.filter(...)), len(cursor.fetchall()) or len(session.query(...).all()) used as a count, or a full list tested with if rows:
javascript: (await Model.find(...)).length or rows.length > 0 after selecting every matching row

any: the query uses COUNT, count(), exists() or LIMIT 1
the loaded rows are also processed, so loading them is needed anyway
the query is bounded to a small fixed number of rows

distinguish_from.PERF-002: the rows are loaded without a limit in order to process them, not just to count them

PERF-020.name: Lock Held Across Slow I/O or an Await Point
PERF-020.question: Does this function hold a lock while it performs slow I/O, sleeps or awaits, so other threads or tasks wait for that whole time?

any: a network request, database query, file read or write, sleep or await runs between acquiring a mutex or exclusive lock and releasing it
python: requests, database or file calls, or await, inside a with lock: block
javascript: an await on a network or database call while an async mutex or lock from a library is held
cpp: I/O or sleep calls inside the scope of a std::lock_guard, std::unique_lock or between lock() and unlock()
c: I/O or sleep calls between pthread_mutex_lock and pthread_mutex_unlock
rust: I/O or .await while a MutexGuard or RwLock write guard is alive

any: the critical section only reads or updates in-memory state, and slow work happens after release
the lock exists specifically to serialise access to that I/O resource, such as one writer to a file

distinguish_from.CWE-833: the lock ordering can deadlock, rather than merely slowing others
distinguish_from.REL-242: a guard or borrow held across an await can deadlock or panic in Rust

PERF-021.name: Busy-Wait Polling Without Sleeping or Blocking
PERF-021.question: Does this function wait for a condition by spinning in a loop that checks it repeatedly without sleeping, blocking or yielding?

any: a loop whose body only re-reads a flag, queue size, file or status until it changes, with no sleep, wait or yield
a loop that spins comparing the current time with a deadline to implement a delay
c: while (!flag) {} or while (!flag); on a volatile or atomic flag with no pause, sched_yield or sleep
cpp: while (!flag.load()) {} on a std::atomic with no std::this_thread::yield, sleep_for or wait
javascript: a while loop on Date.now() to delay, which also blocks the event loop
python: while not done: pass or a loop polling a condition with no time.sleep or Event.wait
rust: loop { if flag.load(..) { break } } with no std::hint::spin_loop, park or sleep for longer than a short spin

any: the loop sleeps, blocks on a wait, select, channel or future, or yields between checks
a bounded short spin precedes a blocking fallback, as in a spinlock with backoff
cpp: std::condition_variable::wait with a predicate, or std::atomic::wait from C++20, blocks until notified

distinguish_from.CWE-835: the loop can never end because its exit condition is unreachable
distinguish_from.CWE-1322: the cost is blocking a single-threaded event loop by any means, not spinning specifically

PERF-022.name: Recursive Recomputation of Overlapping Subproblems Without Memoisation
PERF-022.question: Does this function call itself several times on overlapping arguments without caching results, so the same subproblems are solved again and again?

any: two or more recursive calls on smaller, overlapping arguments, such as f(n - 1) + f(n - 2), with no memo table
a recursive search over positions or substrings that revisits the same state through different paths without remembering it
results are stored in a cache, memo dictionary or table that is checked before recursing
the recursive calls cover disjoint parts of the input, as in merge sort or tree traversal
the input is bounded to a small constant
python: the function is decorated with functools.cache or lru_cache

distinguish_from.PERF-008: the repeated work is an external call or lookup rather than a recursive computation
distinguish_from.CWE-674: the risk is unbounded recursion depth rather than repeated work

PERF-023.name: Full Sequence Materialised Only to Be Scanned Once
PERF-023.question: Does this function build a complete intermediate list or array only to scan it once, such as summing it or testing whether any element matches?

python: sum([...]), any([...]), all([...]), min([...]) or max([...]) with a list comprehension rather than a generator expression
readlines() or list(...) built only to be looped over once
javascript: array.filter(fn).length > 0 or filter(fn)[0] where some or find would stop early
map then a single reduce or forEach over a large array where one pass would do
rust: collect::<Vec<_>>() followed only by .iter() for a single pass, len() or is_empty()

any: the intermediate collection is used more than once, returned or stored
the input is small and bounded
python: a generator expression or itertools pipeline feeds the reduction
javascript: some, every, find or a single reduce is used
rust: the iterator chain is consumed directly with sum, any, count or find

distinguish_from.PERF-002: the whole data set is loaded from a store or file without limit, rather than copied in memory

PERF-024.name: Interleaved DOM Reads and Writes Forcing Repeated Layout
PERF-024.question: Does a loop in this function write to the DOM or element styles and then read layout properties, forcing the browser to recompute layout each pass?

javascript: inside one loop, el.style, className, appendChild or innerHTML is changed and offsetHeight, offsetWidth, clientHeight, scrollTop or getBoundingClientRect is read
tsx: a ref's current element is resized or restyled and measured in the same loop inside an effect

any: all layout reads happen before any writes, or writes are batched in requestAnimationFrame
the loop only writes, or only reads
the code does not run in a browser, for example a Node script

PERF-025.name: Large Multi-Dimensional Array Traversed Against Its Storage Order

sources.standard: What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory (Drepper)

PERF-025.question: Does this function walk a large row-major array or matrix with its innermost loop moving across rows, or multiply large matrices with the naive loop order and no transposition, tiling or library call?

c: for (i...) for (j...) sum += a[j][i] or a[j * n + i] over runtime-sized n
for (i) for (j) for (k) c[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j] over large runtime sizes with no transposed copy of b and no blocking
cpp: nested loops over std::vector<std::vector<T>> or a flat buffer indexed [col][row] in the inner loop
rust: nested loops indexing grid[j][i] or data[j * width + i] with j in the inner loop over runtime-sized dimensions
python: pure Python or Numba loops over a NumPy C-ordered array indexing arr[j, i] with j innermost, or a hand-written triple-loop matrix product

c: the innermost loop walks contiguous memory
the array is small or of fixed tiny size, such as 3 by 3 or 4 by 4
the matrix product transposes one operand, uses blocking or calls BLAS or another library
rust: the inner loop walks a row, iterators over rows or chunks are used, or ndarray or nalgebra performs the product
python: vectorised NumPy operations or @ are used
the array is Fortran-ordered and the loop follows that order

distinguish_from.CWE-1176: the work itself is avoidable, rather than its memory access order being cache-hostile

PERF-026.name: Per-Thread Data Packed Into One Cache Line and Written Concurrently

sources.standard: What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory (Drepper)

PERF-026.question: Does this function have several threads write repeatedly to neighbouring slots or fields of one shared array or struct inside their loops?

c: counts[tid]++ or results[tid] += x inside each thread's main loop, on a plain array of small elements
cpp: std::vector<long> or std::array of per-thread counters updated in each thread's loop, or std::atomic<int> slots packed next to each other
rust: a Vec<AtomicUsize> or array of per-worker counters updated in each worker's loop, or adjacent fields each written by a different thread

c: each thread accumulates in a local variable and writes its slot once at the end
slots are padded or aligned to the cache line, for example alignas(64) or a padding member
the writes are rare compared with the loop's other work
rust: slots use crossbeam CachePadded or #[repr(align(64))]
each worker returns a local total that is combined afterwards

distinguish_from.PERF-027: all threads write one shared variable, rather than separate variables on one line

PERF-027.name: Shared Atomic or Locked Counter Updated on Every Iteration by All Threads

sources.standard: What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory (Drepper)
What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory (Drepper)

PERF-027.question: Does each worker thread in this function update one shared atomic or lock-protected counter on every iteration of its main loop?

c: atomic_fetch_add(&total, 1) or __sync_fetch_and_add on a shared variable for every item processed by each thread
pthread_mutex_lock around a shared counter increment per item
cpp: std::atomic<long> total; total++ or fetch_add per element inside a parallel loop or each std::thread's loop
rust: counter.fetch_add(1, ...) on an Arc<AtomicUsize> per item in each thread, or a Mutex<u64> locked per item in a rayon closure

c: each thread sums locally and updates the shared value once
the shared update happens once per batch or rarely
rust: rayon sum, fold and reduce, or per-thread totals combined at the end
the counter is updated once per batch

distinguish_from.PERF-020: a lock is held across slow I/O rather than taken briefly for each item

PERF-028.name: Linked List Used for Bulk Sequential Traversal Where a Contiguous Array Would Do

sources.standard: What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory (Drepper)

PERF-028.question: Does this function build a linked list only to append to it and then scan or index it sequentially, with no insertion or removal in the middle?

c: a malloc'd node chain built by appending and then walked in full, where an array of the same items would do
cpp: std::list or std::forward_list filled with push_back and then only iterated, or advanced with std::next to reach an index
rust: std::collections::LinkedList filled with push_back and then only iterated

c: items are inserted or removed in the middle while iterating, or splicing is used
the code needs stable addresses for elements while the collection changes
the list is short or built once and rarely traversed
cpp: std::vector or std::deque is used
rust: Vec or VecDeque is used

distinguish_from.PERF-011: an array is used as a queue and shifted on each removal, the opposite trade-off
